questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Canada about 9,984,670 square kilometres; Latvia about 64,594 square kilometres; Kiribati about 811 square kilometres; Dominica about 751 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Ottawa?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Canada is Ottawa.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Canada?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Canada article.

questions.proof: The national capital is Ottawa, and the nation's most populous city is Toronto.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Canada?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Canada on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography and climate” part of the Canada article.

questions.proof: It shares its southern and northwestern land border with the United States.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Canada on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Canada on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
